# Annotated bibliography

51 verified entries. Each was checked against its registry record (Crossref, arXiv, OpenAlex for the abstract), a publisher or patent page, or (marked) the full text; summaries are written from the abstract or the text read. Entries that could not be verified are listed at the end and are not cited in the paper.

## The five papers closest to our contribution

- **xing2018**: Yufei Xing, Jiaxing Dong, Sarvagya Dwivedi, Umar Khan, Wim Bogaerts, "Accurate extraction of fabricated geometry using optical measurement", Photonics Research, vol. 6, no. 11, 1008-1020, 2018, doi:10.1364/prj.6.001008. *How ours differs:* Extracts width and thickness with the angle fixed at an assumed 85 deg; we ask whether the angle itself can be extracted. Its measured local width variation is the scale against which our co-location requirement must be read.
- **lu2017**: Zeqin Lu, Jaspreet Jhoja, Jackson Klein, Xu Wang, Amy Liu, Jonas Flueckiger et al., "Performance prediction for silicon photonics integrated circuits with layout-dependent correlated manufacturing variability", Optics Express, vol. 25, no. 9, 9712, 2017, doi:10.1364/oe.25.009712. *How ours differs:* One of the closest: extraction from resonators assuming the structures share the extracted parameters. We show the angle is invisible to such strips and quantify how the shared-parameter assumption limits an angle extraction.
- **butt2024**: Jordan N. Butt, Nathan F. Tyndall, Marcel W. Pruessner, Kyle J. Walsh, Benjamin L. Miller, Nicholas M. Fahrenkopf et al., "Optical and geometric parameter extraction across 300-mm photonic integrated circuit wafers", APL Photonics, vol. 9, no. 1, 016104, 2024, doi:10.1063/5.0173914. *How ours differs:* Closest in spirit to our parameter set (geometry plus indices); four parameters, no sidewall angle, SiN rather than SOI.
- **nrc2026**: Dan-Xia Xu, Pavel Cheben, Sergey Dedyulin, Siegfried Janz, Jens Schmid, "High accuracy determination of optical waveguide geometry using a single spectral measurement of a dispersive device", WIPO PCT application WO2026097166A1 (National Research Council Canada), 2026, https://patents.google.com/patent/WO2026097166A1/en. *How ours differs:* Closest to our finding on local variation: it avoids multi-device fitting for the same reason our variation analysis exposes. It does not extract the angle.
- **zhang2024**: Enge Zhang, Xiaoran Zhu, Lei Zhang, "Effective and group refractive index extraction and cross-sectional dimension estimation for silicon-on-insulator rib waveguides", Optics Express, vol. 32, no. 18, 31375, 2024, doi:10.1364/oe.534015. *How ours differs:* A rib with a slab, as in our proposal, but the angle is not extracted.

All five extract width, thickness (and, in Butt et al., material indices) from rings or interferometers and hold the sidewall angle at an assumed value or leave it out. None asks whether the angle is identifiable, which structures make it identifiable, or how the shared-parameter assumption limits it; those are the questions of this paper.

## Optical extraction of waveguide geometry

### xing2018

- **Citation:** Yufei Xing, Jiaxing Dong, Sarvagya Dwivedi, Umar Khan, Wim Bogaerts, "Accurate extraction of fabricated geometry using optical measurement", Photonics Research, vol. 6, no. 11, 1008-1020, 2018, doi:10.1364/prj.6.001008
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (full text read, pp. 1008-1020; quotes with pages in results_final/CITATIONS.md)
- **Summary:** Extracts the linewidth and thickness of SOI strip waveguides from n_eff and n_g fitted to a low-order (m ~ 15) and a high-order (m ~ 150) MZI, through a third-order polynomial map from (w, t) to (n_eff, n_g), with total errors of 0.37 nm and 0.26 nm on an imec MPW die. The sidewall angle is fixed at 85 deg, taken from the foundry handbook, and the authors state that the error from the unknown wall shape cannot be compensated, so some extracted parameters are only relative.
- **Cite for:** state of the art of optical geometry extraction; the angle held at a handbook value; measured fitting errors (n_eff 1.1e-5, n_g 1.0e-3); local width variation up to 3 nm between nearby devices
- **Relation to our work:** Extracts width and thickness with the angle fixed at an assumed 85 deg; we ask whether the angle itself can be extracted. Its measured local width variation is the scale against which our co-location requirement must be read.

### liu2025

- **Citation:** Yichen Liu, Umar Khan, Wim Bogaerts, "Accurately extracting silicon waveguide dimensions from a single high-order Mach-Zehnder Interferometer", Optics Express, vol. 33, no. 6, 13530, 2025, doi:10.1364/oe.558406
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from crossref)
- **Summary:** Extracts the dimensions of SOI strip waveguides (imec iSiPP50G) from the n_eff and n_g of a single high-order MZI, with a mapping model from geometry to indices, and discusses the feasibility and the extraction errors.
- **Cite for:** single-MZI extraction of n_eff and n_g, and its error analysis
- **Relation to our work:** Again width and thickness; motivates our question of which readouts add independent information (we find the MZI phase is parallel to the ring n_eff).

### butt2024

- **Citation:** Jordan N. Butt, Nathan F. Tyndall, Marcel W. Pruessner, Kyle J. Walsh, Benjamin L. Miller, Nicholas M. Fahrenkopf et al., "Optical and geometric parameter extraction across 300-mm photonic integrated circuit wafers", APL Photonics, vol. 9, no. 1, 016104, 2024, doi:10.1063/5.0173914
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from crossref)
- **Summary:** Extracts core thickness, width offset and core and cladding indices of silicon nitride waveguides with unbalanced MZIs across a 300 mm wafer, with relative standard deviations of 0.3% (2.6 nm) for the width offset and 0.5% (1.1 nm) for the thickness, and verifies the maps by predicting other devices.
- **Cite for:** wafer-scale multi-parameter extraction and its use for prediction
- **Relation to our work:** Closest in spirit to our parameter set (geometry plus indices); four parameters, no sidewall angle, SiN rather than SOI.

### dwivedi2015

- **Citation:** Sarvagya Dwivedi, Alfonso Ruocco, Michael Vanslembrouck, Thijs Spuesens, Peter Bienstman, Pieter Dumon et al., "Experimental Extraction of Effective Refractive Index and Thermo-Optic Coefficients of Silicon-on-Insulator Waveguides Using Interferometers", Journal of Lightwave Technology, vol. 33, no. 21, 4471-4477, 2015, doi:10.1109/jlt.2015.2476603
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from OpenAlex)
- **Summary:** Measures n_eff and its thermo-optic coefficient over the C-band with three MZIs, accounting for fabrication variability, with wafer-scale maps for 450, 600 and 800 nm wide waveguides.
- **Cite for:** MZI-based index and dispersion extraction
- **Relation to our work:** Uses several interferometers whose shared geometry is assumed; our Monte Carlo and variation analysis test that kind of assumption.

### atsumi2012

- **Citation:** Yuki Atsumi, Dan-Xia Xu, André Delâge, Jens H. Schmid, Martin Vachon, Pavel Cheben et al., "Simultaneous retrieval of fluidic refractive index and surface adsorbed molecular film thickness using silicon wire waveguide biosensors", Optics Express, vol. 20, no. 24, 26969, 2012, doi:10.1364/oe.20.026969
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from OpenAlex)

- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from OpenAlex)

### zhang2024

- **Citation:** Enge Zhang, Xiaoran Zhu, Lei Zhang, "Effective and group refractive index extraction and cross-sectional dimension estimation for silicon-on-insulator rib waveguides", Optics Express, vol. 32, no. 18, 31375, 2024, doi:10.1364/oe.534015
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from crossref)

### nrc2026

- **Citation:** Dan-Xia Xu, Pavel Cheben, Sergey Dedyulin, Siegfried Janz, Jens Schmid, "High accuracy determination of optical waveguide geometry using a single spectral measurement of a dispersive device", WIPO PCT application WO2026097166A1 (National Research Council Canada), 2026, https://patents.google.com/patent/WO2026097166A1/en
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (Google Patents page read 2026-11-03) (abstract from patent claim 1 / abstract on the page)
- **Summary:** Patent application: determines waveguide geometry from multiple consecutive resonances of one ring of known cavity length by constrained regression. Its background states that methods using several devices must assume they share the same width and thickness variations, which "is recognized as often not satisfied", and it treats a non-negligible sidewall angle as an input to the index model.
- **Cite for:** single-ring geometry extraction; the shared-variation assumption stated as a known weakness
- **Relation to our work:** Closest to our finding on local variation: it avoids multi-device fitting for the same reason our variation analysis exposes. It does not extract the angle.

### lu2017

- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from OpenAlex)
- **Summary:** Extracts waveguide width and height with sub-nanometre accuracy from racetrack resonators, maps their wafer statistics, and feeds spatially correlated variations into a layout-aware Monte Carlo circuit simulation.

### orji2018

- **Citation:** N. G. Orji, M. Badaroglu, B. M. Barnes, C. Beitia, B. D. Bunday, U. Celano et al., "Metrology for the next generation of semiconductor devices", Nature Electronics, vol. 1, no. 10, 532-547, 2018, doi:10.1038/s41928-018-0150-9

## Mode solvers, perturbation theory and derivative accuracy

### johnson2002

- **Citation:** Steven G. Johnson, M. Ibanescu, M. A. Skorobogatiy, O. Weisberg, J. D. Joannopoulos, Y. Fink, "Perturbation theory for Maxwell’s equations with shifting material boundaries", Physical Review E, vol. 65, no. 6, 066611, 2002, doi:10.1103/physreve.65.066611
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from OpenAlex)
- **Summary:** Correct first-order perturbation theory for shifted dielectric interfaces, using surface integrals of the unperturbed fields.
- **Cite for:** the boundary-perturbation formula behind R
- **Relation to our work:** Our closed-form R uses this result.

### farjadpour2006

- **Citation:** A. Farjadpour, David Roundy, Alejandro Rodriguez, M. Ibanescu, Peter Bermel, J. D. Joannopoulos et al., "Improving accuracy by subpixel smoothing in the finite-difference time domain", Optics Letters, vol. 31, no. 20, 2972, 2006, doi:10.1364/ol.31.002972
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from OpenAlex)
- **Summary:** Subpixel smoothing of the dielectric function for FDTD, designed from perturbation theory, with quadratic convergence.
- **Cite for:** accuracy of discretized interfaces
- **Relation to our work:** Context for the EMpy derivative errors.

### kottke2008

- **Citation:** Chris Kottke, Ardavan Farjadpour, Steven G. Johnson, "Perturbation theory for anisotropic dielectric interfaces, and application to subpixel smoothing of discretized numerical methods", Physical Review E, vol. 77, no. 3, 036611, 2008, doi:10.1103/physreve.77.036611
- **Verified:** VERIFIED (registry record) (abstract from OpenAlex)
- **Summary:** First-order perturbation theory for shifted anisotropic interfaces, leading to a subpixel smoothing scheme.
- **Cite for:** perturbation theory and subpixel smoothing
- **Relation to our work:** Explains why grid-based derivatives need careful averaging.
